evidence_level: L2 (real firmware + 6DOF plant + sensor models, SIL only)
purpose: Compare 20 s outage (GNSS recovers before touchdown) with 60 s outage (no GNSS recovery before touchdown) at a true 30 m hover; test a conservative baro-altitude-slope vertical-velocity override.
scenario: 30 m target, pos-hold at 41 s, outage 43-103 s, 1 m/s2 wind, 6 directions x 10 seeds; run 133 s

r1.variant: baseline descent + speed hold + alt-hold 6 s

r2.variant: baseline descent + speed hold + alt-hold 6 s

r3.variant: baseline descent + speed hold + alt-hold 6 s

baromin.variant: baseline + 0.5 s baro-slope override when it is >0.5 m/s below EKF vz

caveats: 20 s outage at the same 30 m settled altitude (r1) gives touchdown median/p95/max 0.85/1.02/3.29 m/s; the soft touchdown depends on GNSS recovery before landing.
60 s outage without recovery gives 3.35-3.88 m/s median touchdown for 1/2/3 m/s target ramps; faster ramps do not help.
The baro-slope override reduces touchdown median to 1.84 m/s but increases landing drift median from 432 to 714 m; it is a trade, not a fix, and is not adopted.

A ground-dwell latch (target locked to current altitude after 1 s below 0.3 m) was added after these runs; it prevents the residual 13.4 m climb command after early touchdown but does not change pre-touchdown metrics.
SIL plant has no ground friction/landing gear/impact model; post-landing roll-over under wind is a plant artifact.
All numbers are scalar-Eigen SIL L2, not real aircraft.
